study_families.study_label: BEAT (Immune signature and exercise) acute-exercise high-resolution sampling study, TU Dortmund
study_families.design: Single-arm, repeated-measures acute exercise bout with high-resolution serial venous blood sampling (within-subject, no non-exercise control arm).
study_families.cointerventions: overnight fast before the exercise session (standardisation, not a co-intervention per se)
study_families.study_notes: Published as a short 'Did You Know?' communication in Acta Physiologica; study dashboard at https://sportsmedicine-dortmund.shinyapps.io/beat (p.1,4). Pilot purpose flags 'shared cohort' (靶向蛋白动力学与共享队列) – no other report in this 2-report pilot batch shares this cohort; potential overlap with other TU Dortmund Zimmer/Joisten-group publications outside the pilot set could not be checked within this task's scope (see unresolved_questions).

reports.title: Immunological Protein Signature During Acute Exercise
reports.authors: Wenzel C; Walzik D; Wences T; Trebing S; Meyer K; Groll A; Zimmer P; Joisten N
source_locator: p.1 masthead: Received 10 Sep 2025; Revised 13 Oct 2025; Accepted 14 Oct 2025; Acta Physiologica 2025;241:e70125
reports.inclusion_reason: Single identifiable acute bout (40-min aerobic exercise at 60% VO2peak) with pre-exercise baseline and serial within-window post-exercise/recovery (up to 1 h) samples; targeted immunological protein panel (cytokines, chemokines, effector molecules, immune cell-surface markers) satisfies immune linkage as recognized_immune_mediator.
reports.reviewer_notes: Charting-pilot extraction only; full-text screening disposition belongs to the separate 50-record screening pilot and is out of scope here. See eligibility_opinion for reviewer B's descriptive scope_stream judgement. Note: this is a short 'Did You Know?' format article (4 pages, no separate Methods heading); see unresolved_questions on publication_status/article-type classification.
reports.author_stated_use: 'In conclusion, we identified 44 of 92 immunological proteins displaying significant time-dependent changes. Cluster analysis revealed distinct kinetic patterns, highlighting their dynamic temporal regulation and potential mechanistic interactions.' (p.3) – framed as mechanistic characterisation; no explicit monitoring/diagnostic/clinical-use claim is stated.
author_window_interpretation_locator: Entire text (pp.1-3) contains no use of 'open window', no discussion of immunosuppression/infection susceptibility, and no redistribution/demargination framing; discussion is limited to protein kinetics and IL-6/IL-10, NK-granzyme and growth-factor mechanisms.

precision_validation.replication: No technical replicates, no assay-reliability statistic (ICC/CV/LOD) reported for the Olink panel in this report.
source_locator: p.1 (no reliability statistics reported in the available text)
precision_validation.evidence_notes: No ICC/CV or QC-failure-rate information is reported for the Olink assay in this short communication.

precision_validation.response_evidence: 7 timepoints from pre-exercise baseline through 1h recovery, densely covering during-exercise and within-window post-exercise bins.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: High-resolution kinetic design (baseline, warm-up, 10, 15, 30, 40 min, 1h post) is a direct strength for temporal_validity within the window, but no sampling beyond 1h means the full within-window (up to 72h) recovery trajectory is not charted by this report alone.

source_locator: p.1: 'cytokines, chemokines, effector molecules, cell surface markers, growth factors, and immune regulators'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Panel is explicitly immunology-oriented (Immuno-Oncology panel) but includes non-immune-specific growth factors (FGF2, PDGF-B, EGF, VEGFA), so specificity is mixed/panel-dependent rather than uniformly high across all 92 analytes.

precision_validation.replication: Within-bout repeated sampling of the same 12 participants (not repeated bouts); no cross-bout reliability (ICC/CV) reported.
precision_validation.individualization: 'The t-SNE analysis resulted in distinct clusters for each individual and a separation between male and female participants... immune responses to acute exercise are highly individual and influenced by sex' (p.1).
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Clear qualitative evidence of inter-individual (and sex) differences in protein response patterns (t-SNE clustering by participant ID), but this is within a single bout only; no repeated-bout or formal individual-level reliability/response-heterogeneity statistic (ICC/CV/responder definition) is reported.

precision_validation.functional_evidence: No direct immune-function assay (e.g., NK cytotoxicity assay) performed; NK-granzyme kinetics interpreted only by analogy to a separately cited meta-analysis (ref. 9), not measured here.
source_locator: p.3 cluster 2 paragraph (granzymes/NK discussion, citing ref. 9 rather than own functional data)
precision_validation.evidence_notes: No clinical/infection follow-up and no direct functional assay in this report; protein-level kinetic associations (correlation network, SHAP) are statistical co-measurement/prediction evidence, not direct function or clinical endpoints.

precision_validation.temporal_order: Predictor (protein AUC during exercise) measured before outcome (IL-10 concentration at 1h post); temporal order of predictor->outcome is correct.
precision_validation.prediction_design: Random forest model trained per protein to predict IL-10 concentration at 1h post exercise from 44 significant proteins' AUC during exercise; interpreted via SHAP (p.2-3, Figure 1E,F).
precision_validation.prediction_metrics: Model quality assessed by RMSE (leave-one-out); exact RMSE value NR in the available text. Discrimination/calibration/sensitivity-specificity/net-benefit NR (regression, not classification).
precision_validation.leakage_control: Hyperparameter optimisation via Bayesian search; validation by leave-one-out cross-validation (same 12 participants) – i.e. resampling within the same cohort, not an independent held-out cohort.
source_locator: Figure 1 legend (p.2): 'Model validation was conducted using the leave-one-out method, and model quality was assessed using the root mean square error (RMSE)'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Validation is resampling_same_participants (leave-one-out within the same n=12 cohort); per vocabulary_crosswalks.evidence_state only independent_site_or_cohort validation supports evidence_present for this domain, so this is coded not_demonstrated despite the internal cross-validation performed.

precision_validation.field_feasibility: NR (no discussion of sampling burden, cost, turnaround time or field/real-world use anywhere in the available text)
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Unlike R61, this report does not discuss cost, turnaround time or practical/field feasibility at all; coded NR rather than not_demonstrated because the topic is simply not addressed, not addressed-and-found-lacking.

Supplementary file R46_supp_APHA-241-e70125-s001.xlsx was opened programmatically (openpyxl) to resolve exact LMM effect sizes/p-values for the named-candidate measurement rows, since the main 4-page text reports these only narratively/graphically.

eligibility_opinion.rationale: Single identifiable acute bout (40-min aerobic exercise at 60% VO2peak; p.1) with a pre-exercise baseline and serial within-window post-exercise/recovery samples up to 1h (p.1 paragraph 2), i.e. within the 0-72 h organising window with no exposure threshold required. Targeted immunological protein panel (Olink Immuno-Oncology, cytokines/chemokines/effector molecules/immune regulators; p.1) satisfies the immune-linkage rule as recognized_immune_mediator.

unresolved_questions: Blood matrix (plasma vs serum) for the Olink panel is not stated anywhere in the available main text or the two supplement sheets (Proteins, LMM_results); matrix recorded as NR across all sample_sets rows.
Exact exercise modality (cycling, treadmill, other) is not specified in the available text beyond '40-min aerobic exercise session at 60% VO2peak'; exercise_mode recorded as NR.

Article-type/publication_status classification: this is a 4-page 'Did You Know?' section item in Acta Physiologica, containing genuinely new primary data (n=12 trial) rather than a classic editorial/commentary, but the controlled vocabulary's closest non-'peer_reviewed_version_of_record' option is 'editorial_or_commentary'. Coded as peer_reviewed_version_of_record; manual could usefully add a 'short_report_or_research_letter' category.

Narrative-vs-statistics discrepancy: the main text states IFN-gamma 'falls below baseline levels already 15 min after the onset of acute exercise', but the supplement's LMM shows this timepoint is not statistically significant (adjusted p=0.369); only the 1h-post estimate is significant. Several other proteins (PDGF-B, CCL4, CCL8/IL8) are also significant at only one of six post-baseline timepoints. Manual should clarify whether measurement rows must follow strict per-timepoint statistical significance or may also reflect narrative-described directional trends.

Pilot-purpose note flags this report as sharing a cohort with another publication ('共享队列'); within this 2-report pilot batch no other report originates from the same TU Dortmund group, so cohort overlap could not be checked here and should be verified by D/A against the wider corpus (e.g., the Kurgan et al. 2025 bioRxiv preprint cited as ref. 6, from a different group, is not an overlap candidate).

Row-volume issue: a full 'every named candidate regardless of significance' extraction would require up to 92 proteins x 6 post-baseline timepoints = 552 potential measurement rows; this pilot recorded 1 assay-universe row + 6 representative named-candidate rows (comparison = the single most text-anchored timepoint per protein) rather than the full matrix. Same feasibility concern raised independently for R61.
